reforms.description: The Government implemented measures to promote technological innovation as part of structural policy reforms to enhance economic efficiency and growth potential.
reforms.package_name: 1996 Structural Policy Reforms for Innovation and Growth
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Structural reforms promoting technological innovation are expected to enhance economic efficiency and growth potential.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states measures were 'implemented' but provides no detail; classified as announced due to lack of specificity.
reforms.importance_rationale: General statement of intent without specific mechanisms or budget details; insufficient detail to assess structural significance.
reforms.source_quote: Recent measures to overhaul the unemployment insurance system and promote technological innovation are reviewed in Chapter III.

reforms.description: The 1996 Budget allocated up to C$260 million over three years to be reallocated towards three structural-policy priority areas, including technology and innovation, alongside education and employment opportunities for young Canadians and international trade.
reforms.package_name: 1996 Structural Policy Reforms for Innovation and Growth
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Direct public funding for technology and innovation is expected to support productivity growth and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'allocated' in 1996 Budget, indicating announcement; implementation status not explicitly confirmed.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant budget reallocation (C$260 million over three years) across multiple priority areas including innovation, but not a structural overhaul of the R&D system.
reforms.source_quote: over the next three years spending of up to C$ 260 million will be reallocated in three structural-policy priority areas: education and employment opportunities for young Canadians; technology and innovation; and international trade.

reforms.description: Canada introduced the Technology Partnerships Canada (TPC) programme in 1996 to provide reimbursable financing to firms for close-to-market development of key technologies, promoting public-private partnerships in technology commercialisation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Reimbursable financing for close-to-market technology development accelerates commercialisation and reduces barriers to private-sector innovation investment.
reforms.status_evidence: Text explicitly states 'introduced' and 'was established' in 1996, indicating implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant new instrument for technology commercialisation with public-private partnership structure, but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: In 1996, the government introduced the Technology Partnerships Canada (TPC) programme to provide reimbursable financing to firms for close-to-market development of key technologies.

reforms.description: The Canadian Technology Network (CTN), launched in 1996 as a grouping of industry associations, research organisations, government institutes, and universities, was established to provide firms with quick and easy access to business expertise, advice and information on technology.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: A network providing firms with access to expertise and technology information reduces information asymmetries and facilitates technology adoption and commercialisation.
reforms.status_evidence: Text explicitly states 'launched' in 1996, indicating implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant new institutional mechanism for knowledge transfer and technology support, but primarily an information and advisory network rather than a major structural reform.
reforms.source_quote: The Canadian Technology Network (CTN), a grouping of industry associations, research organisations, government institutes, and universities, was launched in 1996 to provide firms with quick and easy access to business expertise, advice and information on technology.

reforms.description: The Technology Partnerships Programme, a joint initiative of three Research Councils, was established to create partnerships among universities and SMEs for research development and commercialisation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: University-SME research partnerships for commercialisation facilitate knowledge transfer and reduce barriers to innovation adoption by smaller firms.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'was established' but provides no year; classified as announced due to lack of implementation confirmation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant new collaborative mechanism involving multiple Research Councils, but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
reforms.source_quote: The Technology Partnerships Programme, a joint initiative of three Research Councils, aims to create partnerships among universities and SMEs for research development and commercialisation.

reforms.description: Canada reformed its Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit in 1995 by introducing new rules facilitating tax credits for R&D performed by third parties, improving the effectiveness of indirect R&D support.
reforms.package_name: 1995 R&D Tax Credit and Spending Reorientation
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Expanded tax credits for third-party R&D reduce the cost of innovation for firms and improve incentives for applied research and development.
reforms.status_evidence: Text explicitly states 'reformed' in 1995, indicating implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant reform of a major indirect R&D support instrument, improving its effectiveness and scope, but not a structural overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: In 1995, new rules were introduced facilitating tax credits for R&D performed by third-parties.

reforms.description: Canada implemented a major reorientation of government science and technology spending under the 1995 Budget, involving closure of seventeen S&T establishments, consolidation of three S&T facilities in Natural Resources Canada, and a planned reduction of C$600 million in government S&T spending by 1998/99.
reforms.package_name: 1995 R&D Tax Credit and Spending Reorientation
reforms.component_name: Government S&T Spending Reorientation and Consolidation
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Consolidation and closure of S&T establishments may improve efficiency and focus, but the C$600 million spending reduction could constrain research capacity and innovation potential in the short to medium term.
reforms.status_evidence: Text explicitly states 'implemented' under the 1995 Budget with specific actions (closures, consolidations) and planned spending reductions.
reforms.importance_rationale: Major structural reorientation of government S&T infrastructure involving closure of 17 establishments, consolidation of facilities, and substantial budget reduction (C$600 million); represents significant system-wide change.
reforms.source_quote: Under the 1995 Budget, government science and technology spending is to fall by C$ 600 million by 1998/99, and will involve the closure of seventeen S&T establishments and the consolidation of three S&T facilities in Natural Resources Canada.
